Supplies: glass screw-top vials eppendorfs ethanol plant press (large and small) flat forceps pan trap label paper micron pen
Supplies: bloom data sheet pen/pencil plant guides
Supplies: 1m PVC pipes quadrat data sheet pen/pencil plant guides
Supplies: pan traps (5 blue, 5 yellow, 5 white) 1L bottle of water 1mL dish soap kestral weather data sheet pen/pencil/sharpie
Supplies: transect tape field flags flagging tape compass silver sharpie GPS

steps.title: Establish Plot Boundaries and Flags
steps.instruction: Set up three 50m x 50m plots per meadow site using GPS coordinates and cardinal direction flags.

substeps.instruction: Locate plot center via GPS and mark with a red flag labeled with site initials, plot number, and 'C' using a silver sharpie.
Use a compass and transect tape to walk 25m in the four cardinal directions (N, S, E, W) and place flags labeled with site initials, plot number, and direction (e.g., JC1 W).
Use consistent flag colors: Center (Red), West (White), North (Pink), South (Yellow), East (Orange).
Tie a unique color of flagging tape under all flags within a single plot to distinguish between the three plots.
For new sites, mark the center point on the GPS, label it with site initials and plot number (e.g., JC1), and save the point without editing location or elevation.

steps.title: Set Up Pan Traps
steps.instruction: Deploy colored pan traps at every flag for each plot at the start of the sampling day.

substeps.instruction: Prepare soapy water by adding 1mL of dish soap to 1L of water and shaking vigorously.
At each flag, place one white, one yellow, and one blue pan trap, filling each approximately 2/3 full with the soapy water.
Position pans in flat, sunny locations, avoiding tall grass or bushy plants; keep them close enough to the flag for retrieval.

steps.title: Conduct Active Insect Sampling
steps.instruction: Perform 30-minute active sampling rounds for pollinating insects within assigned plots.

substeps.instruction: Verify weather conditions using a Kestral: temperature must be between 17-24°C and windspeed below 2.5 m/s.
Set a stopwatch to 30-minute countdown; stop the timer during capture, jar transfer, and labeling, and restart only when ready to search again.
Collect any pollinating insect (bees, flies, butterflies, wasps) actively foraging on reproductive parts of a flower; ignore non-pollinators (beetles, grasshoppers, ants, ladybugs, spiders).
Transfer specimens to a clean jar labeled with plot number, date, collector initials, sample round (X.Y format), and flower species/description.
Store jars on an ice pack in a fanny pack or tote.
After the round, place insects in a Ziploc bag labeled with site, plot number, sampling round, date, and initials, then store in a dry ice cooler.

steps.title: Collect Plant Vouchers and Samples
steps.instruction: Collect pressed and ethanol-preserved samples for every plant species present on-site.

substeps.instruction: Collect one pressed sample per species including petals, leaves, stem, and roots; label with site, date, and identification.
Collect at least one flower head in ethanol using a large screw-top glass vial or eppendorf (do not use snap-caps); label with site, date, and identification.
Use a 6-letter code for labeling (first three letters of genus and species, e.g., 'HYMHOO').
If flower ID is uncertain, take photos, write a detailed description, and take a pressed specimen for later identification.

steps.title: Perform Vegetation and Bloom Surveys
steps.instruction: Complete quadrat and bloom data sheets for each sampling round.

substeps.instruction: Create a 1m^2 square using PVC pipes at every flag (N, S, E, W, C) and at the halfway points between the center and directional flags (MN, MS, ME, MW).
For each quadrat, identify floral species, assess bloom stage (beginning, fully, or finishing), and count individual plants.
Complete a site-wide bloom data sheet listing every flowering plant per plot, their average bloom stage, and a rough estimate of plant numbers (bins of 10,000).

steps.title: Collect Pan Traps
steps.instruction: Retrieve pan traps after approximately 4.5 to 5 hours of appropriate sampling weather.

substeps.instruction: Adjust retrieval time if weather becomes inappropriate (temp < 17°C, wind > 2.5m/s, rain, or too overcast); record these intervals on the Pan Weather sheet.
Record final weather data on the pan weather sheet.
Collect flying pollinators from each pan and place them in ethanol-filled eppendorf vials with labels (e.g., 'S W' for South White pan).
Use additional vials if necessary, copying all label information exactly.

steps.title: Process Insects in Laboratory
steps.instruction: Process collected insects based on species, ensuring sterile conditions for microbiome assessment.

substeps.instruction: For Bombus and Apis: Wear nitrile gloves washed with bleach and ethanol. Sterilize forceps with bleach, ethanol, and flame. Transfer specimens to 2mL microcentrifuge tubes without touching them or breathing on them. Re-sterilize forceps between every specimen.
Store Bombus/Apis tubes in a labeled Ziploc bag in a -80°C freezer (or on dry ice if the freezer is inaccessible). Do not process these at camping sites.
For all other insects: Pin specimens normally, grouping those with identical label information under a single head label.

steps.title: Sterilize Equipment and Prepare for Next Site
steps.instruction: Clean collection jars and prepare materials for the subsequent field day.

substeps.instruction: Submerge open collection jars in bleachy water for 5-10 minutes, stir to ensure internal contact, rinse with clean water, and air dry overnight (open in car when camping).
Prepare Ziploc bags containing 20 ethanol-filled eppendorfs and one 1mL dish soap eppendorf.
Prepare data sheets: one quadrat and bloom sheet per site, and 23 weather sheets per site (20 for insects, 2-3 for pan traps).
Replace batteries in Kestrals and GPS and organize camping supplies.
